findings.summary: Coverage is explicitly partial and should stay so: affect has additional verb senses (pretend/assume) and a specialized psychology noun; effect has a formal transitive verb and several noun senses; rise has many motion, standing, awakening, noun and idiomatic uses. No omissions should be silently filled by this audit. The draft notes some omissions, which is good, but learners must not read these selected entries as exhaustive.
findings.access: Cambridge search-result excerpts; direct opens returned 403. Coverage concerns are not candidate falsehoods; no omitted sense is proposed as an approved new record.
findings.correction: Keep coverage disclaimer prominent in draft handoff; subsequent bounded scope should explicitly include or exclude additional POS/senses with evidence and homograph review.
findings.editorialDecision: Human lexicographer to decide future coverage and any POS/homograph boundaries.

findings.summary: “Planned” adds an unsupported intention/planning requirement to effect. Standard formal use is to achieve/cause something to happen, as in effect a change. The current example is grammatical but does not establish that planning is an entailment.
findings.access: Cambridge search-index excerpt; MLA content described by candidate metadata and search listing, not independently fetched in this review.
findings.correction: Remove “planned” or record a source-supported contextual restriction; do not otherwise alter candidate automatically.
findings.editorialDecision: Human editor approves exact definition and example fit.

findings.summary: Several definitions are narrower or less idiomatic than the supported core: affect “condition or course” excludes common broad change/influence formulations; effect result is narrow but within declared partial scope; economic “how an economy operates” may understate related-to-money/trade/industry uses; economical resource definition is plausible but its source support is weak.
findings.access: Cambridge search-index excerpts; grammar direct open returned 403.
findings.correction: Consider clearer learner wording only after human editorial review; preserve sense boundaries and contextual distinction.

findings.summary: The scoped transitivity claims and examples are grammatical. Counterexample challenge: raise does not require a human subject (a shortage raised costs); rise may be externally caused while remaining intransitive (costs rose after the shortage). “By itself” should not be used as a causal rule. A passive form (costs were raised) does not make raise lexically intransitive. The batch already avoids the two absolute errors.
findings.access: BBC PDF directly inspected; Cambridge search excerpts. No broad claim over every lemma use is endorsed.
findings.correction: Retain transitivity scoped to selected meanings; use examples that make the direct object evident. Effect example grammatical but formal verb registration should remain explicit.
findings.editorialDecision: Human grammar reviewer should confirm effect valency/register.

findings.summary: All seven are correctly represented as gloss_only; none invents a target Vietnamese sense. Tăng lên/raise and ảnh hưởng/affect fit the selected contexts. Tạo ra, làm tăng, and tiết kiệm are plausible proposals but exact bilingual context/valency evidence was not directly retrievable here. Kết quả is a broad result gloss; tác động is context-sensitive and must not collapse the noun result sense into influence. Thuộc về kinh tế is suitable for economic but cannot cover profitability without another contextual gloss.
findings.access: Search-index excerpts for affect, rise and economic; effect and raise direct fetch 403 and no exact gloss excerpt was verified. Cambridge translations identify PASSWORD © K Dictionaries 2015 for some entries; access is not reuse permission.
findings.correction: Keep unverified glosses explicitly provisional; obtain independent bilingual review and source-specific context before reuse. Do not promote to sense_aligned.
findings.editorialDecision: Vietnamese lexicographer must review sense, collocation and POS scope.

findings.summary: All six examples are original editorial candidates, not attestations. The first four are grammatical and contextually plausible. “Economic pressures.” and “A printer economical with ink.” are fragments: acceptable as collocation snippets, weaker as standalone usage examples. The latter construction is grammatical but somewhat compressed/formal.
findings.access: Example assessment is editorial grammar judgment; no source examples copied or corpus evidence claimed.
findings.correction: Consider full original sentences showing economic usage and economical resource-saving usage; label as editorially authored.

findings.summary: 11 Evidence records are not 11 independent proofs. They are draft, unreviewed, independence unestablished, and many point to the same few sources. Claims cover narrow field paths; exact evidence does not establish the entire sense, examples, gloss, completeness, or publication rights. Search snippets and candidate claims that another parent inspected sources do not authenticate current-source provenance.
findings.access: BBC directly inspected; MLA/Oxford/Cambridge source access classes are recorded per source; direct page responses of 403 are explicitly unavailable.
findings.correction: Before publication, independently verify exact source edition/location and claim support, bind evidence to exact candidate values, and obtain trusted review.
findings.editorialDecision: No editorial authority present; evidence remains unreviewed.
